 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Millwall take on Portsmouth at the weekend, and Alex Neil has a decision to make about who starts to get their promotion charge back on track.
 Millwall currently sit 12th in the Championship. The Lions would have hoped for a better start after 11 games, but with their injury crisis, they can't have too many complaints about their league position.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Alex Neil's side arguably put in one of their poorest performance in well over a year against Lincoln City , but managed to come back from two goals down to rescue a point. There are desperate improvements needed for the South London outfit's next game.
 Photo by Timmy96, via Wikimedia Commons, licensed under CC0 1.0 Universal.
 Millwall face Portsmouth on Saturday, who are one place below them in the table. The Lions must pick up three points to end their run of one win in their last five, and Neil has a decision to make about who will start at Fratton Park.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement How Millwall should line up vs Portsmouth
 After their poor display against Lincoln City , the Lions' head coach must make changes to his side. He should still stick with the 4-2-3-1 shape to match how Portsmouth set up.
 With Filip Marschall confirmed to be out for a significant period, Max Crocombe is the only choice to start in goal for Millwall . The back four should remain unchanged despite a poor record of 18 goals conceded this term. At right-back, Tristan Crama should make just his second start following an injury in pre-season. With Zak Sturge retaining his spot on the left-side.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In the centre of defence should be the usual partnership of Caleb Taylor and Jake Cooper. Following his goal against the Imps last weekend, the Lions' captain is one goal away from leading the Championship for goals scored as a centre-back.
 Jake Cooper's stats for Millwall
 Jenson Metcalfe and Derek Mazou-Sacko should retain their spots in midfield, but another poor performance could see either of them dropped for the next game. On the left wing, Lisbie should make his fourth consecutive start following his first goal for Millwall last week.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Camiel Neghli should be moved to the right wing to allow Luke Cundle a spot in the advanced midfield role following his superb cameos off the bench. Up top, Lyndon Dykes must start, with a current lack of options available in his position.
 The Verdict: Millwall cannot panic after Lincoln City performance
 Millwall were especially awful during the first half against Lincoln City . However, there is every reason to believe that they can come good this season. Although Neil 's side have conceded 18 goals in the league, they have the joint second-most clean sheets this term with four.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Lions also have the fourth-highest xG with 20.5 from 11 games, and they have created the second-most chances with 39. The main problem that the South London outfit have is that they are not finishing their opportunities. They have missed 39 big chances this term.
 Millwall do have a tough test away from home on Saturday. However, they are unbeaten in their last two on the road and a win should give them a needed boost for the next few weeks.
